long_biography.plain_text:
Born Henry Warren Beaty in Richmond, Virginia, Beatty grew up in an educator family with theatrical ambitions. His older sister Shirley MacLaine was already a film star when he left Northwestern, supported himself with low-paid work in New York and studied with Stella Adler. Broadway brought a Tony nomination before Splendor in the Grass established him on screen.

Beatty used his standing as a leading man to expand into authorship and production, most decisively with Bonnie and Clyde. The Academy later recognised a range few filmmakers matched: he earned nominations as actor, writer, director and producer for the same picture on two occasions. Reds won him the directing Oscar in 1982, while the Academy also gave him its Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award. His wealth emerged from sustained film work rather than a single company or inherited holding.
